messages:
devon: Quick q — how should the paged/blocked KV cache expose eviction semantics to attention kernels? we're seeing perf cliffs when fragmentation + kernel prefetch interact.

natalie: tl;dr: kernels today assume dense KV slices. when a page is evicted the kernel ends up issuing synchronous fetches which blows up tail latency.

mike: Confirmed on my repro — 2x tail latency at 2048 context with 16KB page size and random eviction pattern. looks like kernel fetch path is very sensitive to scatter misses.

tara: Proposal: add a small kernel->cache API surface: (1) prefetch/pin hints, (2) acceptable staleness window, (3) hotspot markers for compaction. this lets cache choose pin vs async backfill.

devon: Sketch of proto in plain terms: ``{ hint_window_tokens: 64, staleness_ms: 50, max_sync_miss: 4 }`` kernel sends per-request. cache uses it to decide pin/async/read-ahead.

natalie: Love the shape. Also need a compaction hint: kernel can mark ranges as "hot" so cache avoids scattering them across pages during compaction.

mike: Alternate pattern: kernel exposes an iterator of KV ranges it will touch next. cache uses iterator to coalesce reads (read-ahead) instead of guessing.

bench-bot: perf snapshot (local): master w/ sync fetch: p95 120ms, p99 420ms | with prefetch-iterator prototype: p95 45ms, p99 110ms. test config: 4x batch, 2048 context, 16KB pages.

infra-bot: FYI: cache already has soft-pin + async backfill support deployed in 1750000000, but no kernel hints are wired.

tara: Edge tradeoff: over-eager prefetching for sparse attention patterns will bloat GPU memory and hurt other requests. we need budget controls.

natalie: Add cost budget to hint: e.g. ``{ tokens_preload: 128, bytes_budget: 1MB }``. cache enforces budget and gracefully degrades.

devon: Eviction policy discussion: LRU is simple but fragments. we should do size+age with periodic compaction that coalesces contiguous small slots before evicting.

mike: Compaction must be background and non-blocking. propose compaction epochs with a lease token so kernels can verify indices are still valid (avoid desync during compaction).

tara: Lease format idea: ``{ epoch_id: 42, lease_ttl_ms: 200 }`` kernel checks lease before using an index; if expired, kernel triggers safe fallback.

natalie: Also important: kernel routing based on access pattern. attention kernels that are sequential/sliding-window can be routed to a "pinned-page" runtime variant that ensures locality.

devon: Implementation plan (proposed): 1) add hint proto and runtime plumbing 2) iterator API for coalesced read-ahead 3) background compaction service + lease semantics 4) routing rules in scheduler 5) tests + p99 targets.

mike: Tests to add: synthetic fragmentation patterns, adversarial eviction sequences, integration with attention kernel microbench (8x batch, 4096 context).

bench-bot: Filed perf ticket INFR-3421 and attached initial numbers from earlier.

devon: Question on backward compatibility: if a kernel doesn't send hints, do we default to current behaviour (sync on miss) or assume async/read-ahead? I vote keep conservative default (= sync) to preserve correctness.

natalie: Agreed: default to sync for correctness. enable feature-flag to allow async-conservative mode for controlled experiments.

tara: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up capturing the API examples, compaction design, and routing implications. tagging @natalie @mike for review.

infra-bot: created doc: internal:/infra/rfcs/kv-prefetch-hints-1765432100 (links require intranet access).

mike: ack. will mock minimal kernel changes and push a WIP PR to eng-runtime tomorrow.

devon: Thanks all. follow-ups: add microbench harness, slot adversary tests, and pick a release window. :tada:
